request: Analyze GSE97084 for PMID 28273480 (Enhanced Protein Translation Underlies Improved Metabolic and Physical Adaptations to Different Exercise Training Modes in Young and Old Humans.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (TruSeq v2, HiSeq 2000) of vastus lateralis biopsies at 1000 hr, baseline and 72 hr after the last bout of 12 weeks training (S4.4.1.p1, S1.p3)
final.primary_estimand: within-subject change in muscle gene expression after 12 weeks of training (post vs pre), separately for each training mode (HIIT, RT, CT) within each age group (Young 18-30, Old 65-80) (S2.4.p1, FIG4 A-F)
planned_contrasts: Old HIIT post vs pre (FIG4B; paper: 553 genes increased, S2.4.p2/S2.6.p5)
Young RT post vs pre (FIG4C; 35% fewer up genes than young HIIT, S2.4.p1)
Old RT post vs pre (FIG4D; 70% fewer up genes than old HIIT, ~166)
Young CT post vs pre (FIG4E; 28% fewer up genes than young HIIT)
Old CT post vs pre (FIG4F; 84% fewer up genes than old HIIT, ~88)
Baseline Old vs Young (S2.4.p1; 267 lower + 166 higher in old = 433), associational
final.repeated_measure_unit: participant (pre and post biopsy from the same person)
final.inclusion: all participants with RNA-seq at both timepoints; CT pre-training = post-SED biopsy (B), the pre-SED (A) biopsy is not deposited
final.paper_method: not stated for RNA-seq (MapRSeq pipeline, 'as previously described (Lanza et al., 2012)'); comparisons are per mode-by-age pre vs post

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.1.p2: randomized to HIIT/RT/CT within age groups; S1.p3 and S2.4.p1: RNA-seq at baseline and post-training; FIG4 A-F gives six training-induced DEG sets by mode and age; S4.4.1.p1 gives the threshold (FDR-corrected p <= 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 0.5). The DE software is not named. S2.4.p1 gives baseline age differences (267/166). Only up counts are reported for training contrasts.

vastus lateralis, Homo sapiens, Young/Old x HIIT/Resistance/Combined x Pre/PostTraining matches S2.1
Mayo Clinic submitter matches the study site
103 deposited samples in two count files, all present in metadata

ownership.reasoning: GEO series GSE97084 extraction protocol text is identical to the paper's gene expression methods (S4.4.1.p1) and the factors match the trial design (S2.1.p2).

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns were renamed by prep_merge_counts.py to the sample code (e.g. 10B, 18A) that starts each GEO title; key derived from title by regex and matched exactly. Subject = leading number of the code (10B/10C are the same CT participant; letter = visit). cohort = age x mode for stratified paired fits.

final.source: GSE97084_GeneCount_raw.tsv.gz + GSE97084_GeneCount_raw_2.tsv.gz merged on Ensembl GeneID
final.paper_input: raw reads per gene from MapRSeq

matrix.reasoning: All values integers, library sizes 14-72M; GEO data_processing: 'tab-delimited text files of raw reads per gene in each sample' (MapRSeq). Raw counts suit a negative-binomial model.

design.subject: subject

final.analysis_type: paired pre/post within each age x mode stratum

candidates.value: pooled training (all modes) post vs pre
candidates.reason_rejected: paper reports each mode and age separately (FIG4 A-F); pooling changes the estimand

candidates.value: one joint model with mode x age x time interaction
candidates.reason_rejected: paper compares mode-specific sets by overlap, not by interaction tests; per-stratum paired fits reproduce FIG4

design.reasoning: Each participant has pre and post biopsies (S2.1.p2: baseline and post-training studies in all participants); FIG4 A-F are post vs pre within each mode x age. Time is the factor, subject the blocking key, cohort a stratum. Baseline Old vs Young (S2.4.p1) is a cross-sectional associational comparison on pre-training biopsies.

covariates.disposition: blocking term in every paired fit (~ subject + time)

covariates.disposition: count-file/sequencing batch is constant within subject, so absorbed by subject in paired fits; added only in a sensitivity run of the unpaired baseline age comparison

covariance.reasoning: Repeated measures: pre and post from the same participant, so subject is blocked. The two deposited count files (different library depths) split subjects, not timepoints, so batch is nested in subject.

final.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2 Wald, ~ subject + time, per stratum, complete pairs)

deviations: DE software not named in paper; DESeq2 paired model used
paper may have analyzed all participants rather than complete pairs; we keep complete pairs only (Young CT subject 27 has no post sample)

threshold.reasoning: S4.4.1.p1: FDR-corrected p <= 0.05 and absolute log2 fold change >= 0.5 (inclusive). FIG4 legend repeats it. Audit: FDR < 0.05 only.
